title: Evidence
audience: a law student in a U.S. JD program
purpose: Apply the Federal Rules of Evidence: relevance and its limits, character evidence, impeachment, hearsay and its exceptions, the Confrontation Clause, privileges, lay and expert opinion, authentication and the best evidence rule.
primary_reading: Cornell LII: Federal Rules of Evidence

weeks.2: Special relevance rules: remedial measures, settlements and pleas
weeks.4: Habit and other acts under Rule 404(b)
weeks.7: Hearsay: the definition and non-hearsay uses
weeks.8: Statements excluded from hearsay under Rule 801(d)
weeks.12: Privileges, authentication and the best evidence rule

blocks.deliverable: Rule on relevance objections in a short transcript.
Decide the admissibility of five uses of character evidence.
Plan the impeachment of a witness with prior convictions and statements.
Week 7 midterm; classify ten statements as hearsay or not hearsay.
Apply Crawford v. Washington to testimonial statements.
Apply Rule 702 and Daubert to a proposed expert.
Submit the project; take an unseen 180 minute final in week 14.

project: Trial evidence file: from a supplied case file, write motions in limine on three evidence issues and a ruling memo on every objection in a supplied transcript.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
